title: POV: You Win the Lottery (Most Winners Don't Keep It)
hook: The bell over the door doesn't ring — someone's holding it shut. Six years ago you bought a two-dollar ticket at this same counter. Four hundred twelve million dollars later, you're back — and the odds were never the part that should have scared you.
body: POV: you're an ordinary forklift operator who wins a $412,000,000 Powerball jackpot on your father's birthday numbers — and lives through what the real research says actually happens next, not the movie version. Real, verified mechanics woven in: the real Powerball jackpot odds (1 in 292,201,338); the real lump-sum cash-option haircut (roughly half the advertised jackpot, before any tax); the real federal withholding (24% automatic, 37% top bracket — meaning more is owed at filing); and the episode's central twist — the number everyone repeats, “70% of lottery winners go broke,” is not a real, sourced statistic (the organization it's constantly misattributed to has said on the record it never produced it). The real, peer-reviewed finding is quieter and scarier in a different way: modest winners, already financially precarious before they won, file for bankruptcy at a higher rate within three to five years — winning didn't fix the hole, it just made the hole big enough to be a headline. This episode's “curse” beats are a dramatized recombination of three real, well-documented winners' stories (a robbery-and-lawsuit spiral, a family bankruptcy, a predatory-advisor tragedy) — the protagonist, Dale, Renn, Mateo, and Priya are a fictional composite; no real winner is depicted as fact. Watch the whole series — every life, every level, every way the number costs you. For educational and entertainment purposes.
